Reviewer note: object-id binding is enforced here at the application layer via a `sealedPayload{ObjectID, Data}` wrapper checked after decrypt, because `envelope.Encrypt` accepts an `objectID` it validates but never folds into its AAD (`headerBytes` authenticates only Version/Tenant/DEKID/Algorithm/Nonce). title: Verify and repair artifact-byte integrity
section: 35. Artifact bytes and customer-data onboarding
red: Bit rot/generation swap/missing/partial replica becomes quarantined/unavailable
green: Repair uses only verified copy and retains identity plus immutable verification receipt
refactor: Keep the tested contract behind its semantic owner, remove duplication and rerun the named unit, integration, conformance, race, fuzz, security and recovery suites that apply without changing observable behavior
evidence: `TestTodo_ARTIFACT_006` (a healthy object verifies clean and the receipt names object, generation, location, outcome and time; a caller mutating a returned receipt cannot alter the stored log), `_Fault` with four subtests (BitRot, GenerationSwap, MissingReplica, PartialReplica -- each quarantines and `Get` fails with `errors.Is` matching both `ErrQuarantined` and the specific sentinel rather than serving suspect bytes), `_Integration` (repair from a verified second replica restores service and preserves identity, then with every replica corrupted both `Repair` and `RepairAny` refuse with `ErrNoVerifiedReplica` and the object stays quarantined), `_Race` (50 goroutines mixing Verify and Repair, asserting exact repaired-receipt counts and that 50 concurrent reads afterwards all return identical correct plaintext) and `FuzzTodo_ARTIFACT_006` (2,058,587 execs over 30s, 85 interesting inputs, no crasher; oracle is that arbitrary corruption must never report `OutcomeVerified`) in `internal/store/object` (`integrity.go`: `IntegrityStore`, `evaluateReplica`, `Receipt`, sentinels `ErrQuarantined`/`ErrBitRot`/`ErrGenerationSwap`/`ErrReplicaMissing`/`ErrReplicaPartial`/`ErrNoVerifiedReplica`; `sealed.go` gains `PutNewGeneration`); no migration required. Ground truth is read live from `Stat` and never from anything a replica claims about itself, which is what makes a self-consistent but stale replica detectable. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/store/object/` PASS at 75.9%, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Reviewer-found defect, fixed: `Repair` called the exported `Verify`, which releases the mutex, and then re-read the source replica under a second lock -- a concurrent `PublishReplica` landing in that window would have made repair copy bytes nothing had verified, breaking the one guarantee the GREEN clause states. Evaluation and copy now happen under a single lock hold using the pure `evaluateReplica`, so the bytes written are byte-for-byte the ones that passed

title: Unify endpoint idempotency, expected revision, ETag and conflict semantics
section: 60. Canonical gRPC services, grpcbridge HTTP endpoints and endpoint TDD
red: mismatched header/message idempotency keys pass, same key with changed payload reuses success, concurrent transports create two logical intents/effects, stale `If-Match`/expected revision commits or retry after ambiguous response duplicates work

evidence: `TestEndpointIdempotencyAndRevisionParityUnderConcurrentReplay` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field: concurrent replay across both transports yields one effect and identical outcomes, and a stale revision refuses the write while naming the current one), `TestTodo_ENDPOINT_004_Property` (the digest is stable, total and order-independent, and its length-prefixed field encoding makes `("ab","c")` and `("a","bc")` hash differently so concatenation cannot collide across field boundaries; blank scope fields are refused with `ErrScopeRequired`), `TestTodo_ENDPOINT_004_Race` (the winning goroutine blocks mid-effect so the other fifteen are provably waiting on the stored record rather than racing past it), `TestTodo_ENDPOINT_004_Integration` (header-keyed and message-keyed paths shown to agree through the existing `Compare`/`Vector` parity harness), `TestTodo_ENDPOINT_004_Fault` (a retry after an ambiguous effect replays the stored error rather than re-running the work), `TestTodo_ENDPOINT_004_Security` (three subtests proving principal, tenant and capability each independently prevent a same-key same-payload collision into another caller's stored result), `TestTodo_ENDPOINT_004_Conformance` (five subtests over the revision precondition, including that a zero expected or current revision is never a match) and `TestTodo_ENDPOINT_004_Mutation` (four subtests -- amount changed, field added, field removed, field re-typed -- each returning `*PayloadConflict` rather than the prior success, with a final exact replay showing the effect counter still at one) in `internal/transport/endpoint` (`idempotency.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/transport/endpoint/` PASS at 79.0% with every pre-existing ENDPOINT-006/007/008/009, EP-REG-001 and EP-INTENT-001/002/004 test unchanged, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The header and message keys are unified before hashing: if both are present and disagree the request is refused with `ErrIdempotencyKeyMismatch`, and the resolved key is hashed together with the principal/tenant/capability scope so the same logical request over HTTP and over the message path resolves to one digest. An exact replay returns the stored outcome rather than re-executing -- the distinction is observable because the effect counter stays at one -- while the same key with a changed payload returns `*PayloadConflict` without touching the effect at all, which is the clause a key-only cache would silently fail. `ExpectedRevision` is a `*uint64` so "no precondition requested" stays distinct from "expected revision zero", and a zero on either side is refused rather than treated as a match. The executor closes its ready channel in a defer, so a failing effect can never strand the waiters

title: Implement GetExecutionReceipt and ExportIntentEvidence endpoints
section: 60. Canonical gRPC services, grpcbridge HTTP endpoints and endpoint TDD

evidence: `TestEvidenceEndpointsEnforcePurposeRedactionManifestAndOperationSemantics` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Property`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Golden`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Race`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Integration`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Fault`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Security`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Conformance` and `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Mutation` in `internal/transport/evidence` (`server.go`, `receipt_handler.go`, `export_handler.go`, `crypto.go`, `lineage.go`, `types.go`, `memory.go`), composing `internal/evidence.Assemble`/`Verify`/`Redacted` (EVIDENCE-001), `internal/transport/operations.Record`/`Store` for the long-running operation, `internal/operations/export` for artifact rendering (EXPORT-001) and `internal/cryptoagility` for signing; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/transport/evidence/` PASS at 78.0%, with `./internal/transport/manifest/` 88.3%, `./internal/transport/operations/` 67.5% and `./internal/evidence/` 90.6% all still passing; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED and driftgate, apigate, substratecoverage, enginecoverage, racepolicy, traceability and intentcoverage all pass on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The ambient-data clause is proven by a test that can actually fail. An export reads `LineageSource.Snapshot` exactly once and every downstream artifact derives from that one read; the test injects a lineage source that returns different content on every call and counts them, so an implementation that re-read its source mid-run produces a manifest disagreeing with its own artifacts and is caught. Verified failable by injecting that exact regression, which failed with `lineage source read 2 times during one export`, and passing again on revert. Package integrity is layered and real, not stubbed: `OpenAndVerify` checks the `cryptoagility` signature, then the AES-256-GCM authentication tag, then the manifest digest, then each artifact digest; the Security test flips a ciphertext byte, strips the signature and decrypts with a wrong key, and all three are rejected. Formula injection is neutralised in the human artifact and the exact bytes preserved in the machine artifact, tested with payloads beginning `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab and carriage return. The six lineage hops are asserted individually -- omitting any one, and separately marking any one ABSENT, both fail the export closed -- rather than by a non-empty check. The export returns an operation reference before the archive is built, and the same request twice returns one operation, proven under 32 concurrent callers. **A genuine contract gap, reported rather than forced.** `GetExecutionReceiptResponse.execution_receipt.receipt` is wire-typed `ZeroEffectReceipt`, whose own constructor rejects a non-zero effect count and whose `ReceiptMode` admits only PREFLIGHT and SIMULATE. This todo's RED clauses describe `internal/evidence.BusinessExecutionReceipt` -- a closed, executed intent, where effects are legitimately present. Placing one inside the other would either misstate the effect count or leave the message's declared invariant unchecked, so `GetExecutionReceipt` serves only genuine zero-effect records and the full lineage-bearing receipt is carried by `ExportIntentEvidence`'s operation result, whose `CanonicalDigestReference` exists for exactly that. Closing this properly needs a proto change and is out of a lane's reach. **Boundaries.** The four ports have in-memory implementations only and `EvidenceService` is registered in no composition root, so these endpoints are contract-complete but not yet reachable in a running server; escalated. Key custody is out of scope -- the signer and package key are supplied directly, with no rotation or KMS policy. The zero-source-mutation proof counts writes to the two writable ports and relies on `LineageSource` exposing no write method; it is weaker than the SQL-parsing proof used for EP-WORK-003 and should be strengthened once real adapters exist. The Integration test reaches a real gRPC server and interceptor chain over bufconn but no database. No race detector is available on this host, so the Race entry is a 32-goroutine determinism test rather than a `-race` run

section: 60. Canonical gRPC services, grpcbridge HTTP endpoints and endpoint TDD

evidence: `TestWorkItemClaimReleaseEndpointsAreExclusiveVersionBoundAndIdempotent` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Race` (real goroutines, exactly one winner, stable across five repeated runs), `TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Security`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Conformance`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Fault` (two subtests, including five identical requests producing one effect and one CLAIMED row), `TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Integration` in `internal/transport/humanwork`, and `TestWorkItemClaimCurrentAndReleaseEnforceCurrentAuthority` (six subtests), `TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Property` and `TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Mutation` in `internal/humanwork/workitem` (`claim_release.go`); no migration required -- the RPCs, their generated types and the `forbid_mutation`/RLS scaffolding all pre-existed. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/transport/humanwork/` PASS at 78.7% and `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/workitem/` PASS at 76.9%, both with every pre-existing EP-WORK-001 and WORK-00x test unchanged, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. ENDPOINT-004's `Coordinator` is composed rather than forked, so exact replay and the stale-revision precondition reuse one mechanism. Exclusivity is two-layered by design: the coordinator's precondition check refuses many concurrent losers early with a stale revision, and anyone slipping past is caught by the existing `Store.Claim` `UPDATE ... WHERE item_version = $n` compare-and-swap; no second CAS was written. Append-only assignment evidence is enforced three ways and proven directly: the write paths only ever INSERT into `work_item_transition`, the database grants refuse a raw UPDATE or DELETE (`TestTodo_EP_WORK_002_Mutation` executes one and asserts `permission denied for table work_item_transition`), and migration 00017's `forbid_mutation` trigger stands behind both. Two boundaries recorded rather than glossed. First, `Invocation` discards raw transport headers after admission, so only the message-level idempotency key reaches the handler and `CanonicalDigest`'s header/message folding is not exercised at this call site; replay and revision behaviour are unaffected. Second, production composition is not connected: `internal/transport/cell/cell.go` builds `transporthumanwork.Dependencies` at two sites with only a read port in scope, so `Claims` and `Idempotency` are nil and both endpoints fail closed with UNAVAILABLE in production. Wiring them needs a write port threaded through `buildEdgeHandlerWithDependencies` and its callers, which is outside this todo's file roots and is raised separately. Two `TestTodo_EP_WORK_001_Conformance` cases asserting that Claim and Release return the P1B stub `FAILED_PRECONDITION` were removed because implementing them made those assertions false; the Complete and DecideApproval stub cases remain, and both methods are now covered by their own suite

red: stale task/proposal digest, expired session/claim/delegation, changed manager/SoD, missing required evidence or duplicate/mutated decision completes; restricted evidence appears in response; approval itself executes the business change
green: method rechecks identity/assurance/AuthZ/claim/proposal/decision receipt/SoD, appends exactly one typed completion/approval result and signal, returns current work/intent state/evidence and performs zero domain mutation until workflow/transaction execution

evidence: `TestWorkCompletionAndApprovalEndpointsRejectStaleProposalAuthorityAndDuplicateDecision` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Property`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Golden`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Race`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Integration`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Fault`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Security`, `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Conformance` and `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003_Mutation` in `internal/transport/humanwork` (`ep_work_003_test.go`), plus `TestTodo_EP_WORK_003` and the same matrix in `internal/humanwork/workitem` (`decide_approval.go`, `decide_approval_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/transport/humanwork/` PASS at 82.0% and `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/workitem/` PASS at 76.7%, both with every pre-existing EP-WORK-001/002 and WORK-00x test still passing, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The clause that defines this todo -- approval must not itself execute the business change -- is proven by absence rather than asserted: a `countingExecutor` wraps the real `dbport.Tx`, parses every mutating statement's target table against real PostgreSQL, and the Integration test iterates all recorded writes and fails on any table it does not name, with `work_item` and `work_item_transition` each asserted at exactly one write. A write to a ledger, a budget reservation or an org-chart row would fail by name. Restricted evidence is kept out of responses structurally -- the wire `WorkItem` message carries no evidence field and `ApprovalDecisionResult` carries only ids, revision, decision, reason, principal and timestamp -- and a canary evidence id supplied on a completion request is asserted never to appear anywhere in the marshalled response. Two corrections made along the way. `prepareMutation` required `Dependencies.Claims != nil` for all four mutating methods including the two that never use it; the check is narrowed to the dependencies actually shared and `ClaimWorkItem`/`ReleaseWorkItem` keep their own guards, with the EP-WORK-002 suite confirmed unchanged. Read as a pure sizing model rather than a load test, which is what RED's "persist zero authoritative rows, business events, outbox entries, human work and provider requests" clause requires: the 100k+ timer drain is a dimension the model bounds (`MinTimerBacklogCapacity`), not an action any test performs, so nothing here starts PostgreSQL or generates load. Storage covers rows, index bytes, WAL bytes, locks, connection pool and vacuum seconds; timers cover backlog, drain rate and drain budget; artifacts cover named object classes each with throughput and memory. Every dimension is a `Dimension{Capacity, Measured}` whose zero value or empty unit is rejected as `MISSING_OR_INVALID` rather than read as within budget, and `ratio` additionally guards a non-positive limit so headroom can never divide by zero. Headroom, a rollover point at 80% of capacity and the hard limit are derived per dimension, and a model missing any dimension is rejected outright with no partial completion

ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` -- never a SELECT that precedes the write. Two concurrent transactions may both read no conflict; only one can commit, because PostgreSQL evaluates the index as part of each INSERT's own commit. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race` proves it with 12 goroutines on genuinely independent connections and transactions released from a common barrier, each presenting a distinct idempotency key so the test measures exclusion between different requests rather than deduplication of one retry, and asserts exactly one admission plus a durable row count rather than merely the absence of an error. evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Security`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Race` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Mutation` in `internal/workflow/steps/approval` (`promoux003_test.go`, `promoux003_race_test.go`, `promoux003_mutation_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Integration` in `internal/humanwork/workitem` (`promoux003_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux003_test.go`); new `internal/humanwork/approverclass`, `internal/humanwork/workitem/separation.go`, `internal/humanwork/workitem/disposition.go`, `internal/workflow/steps/approval/authority_recheck.go` and `internal/humanwork/productui/approval_disposition.go`; no migration required, because the guarantee is row locking over the existing `work_item` table rather than a new one. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 75.2% (`internal/workflow/steps/approval`), 75.6% (`internal/humanwork/workitem`), 100.0% (`internal/humanwork/approverclass`), 94.4% (`internal/workflow/promotionexec`), 76.1% (`internal/platform/execution`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`) and 43.5% (`internal/intent/app`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised, not lowered); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The concurrent double-approval is made impossible by the database rather than by a check that precedes the write. `Store.LockApprovalSiblings` issues `SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id AND proposal_ref AND kind='APPROVAL' ORDER BY work_item_id FOR UPDATE` inside the caller's own transaction; ordering by `work_item_id` means every caller acquires the same locks in the same order, so two racing completions cannot deadlock, and because both requirements on one proposal name the _same_ row set only one transaction can hold them. `approval.Complete` takes that lock before it reads any state and before the completing write, and holds it for the rest of the call, so the loser blocks until the winner commits and then observes the committed conflict and refuses with `ErrSeparationConflict`. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Race` proves it with two real PostgreSQL connections and transactions released from a barrier, stable across five runs. RED's undifferentiated-owner clause is closed structurally rather than by convention: the new `approverclass` package derives provably distinct finance and manager principals from one base, and both `internal/platform/execution` and `internal/intent/app` route each requirement to its derived owner instead of the shared `principal:promotion-approver` the dev environment had been minting for both. Digest preservation under reassignment is proven by diff rather than by a non-empty check: the Integration test captures the full durable record, forces a real reassignment through the HRBP departure fallback, then requires `ProposalRef` equality plus field-by-field equality of tenant, item id, kind, work type, correlation, instance, node, requirement ref, policy route, visibility, org scope, deadline, created-at and subjects -- while asserting the owner actually moved, so the equality claim cannot pass vacuously. REFACTOR's clause that separation is evaluated by the approval owner rather than by whichever surface calls it is proven with the UI entirely absent: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Security` drives a conflicted principal through `workitem.Store.DecideApproval` composed with the new `SeparationAuthority` driver -- no HTTP, no journey engine, no page -- and every PRIMARY and RACE subtest calls `approval.Complete` directly. `SeparationAuthority` fills the concrete `workitem.AuthorityRecheckPort` seam that EP-WORK-003 left unimplemented and whose absence was recorded as a boundary when that todo closed. Presentation consumes the disposition rather than recomputing it. `ApprovalDispositionProjectionFrom` is a pure field copy and `approvalDispositionCardProps` only localizes; no membership, authority or conflict logic exists in `productui`. The rendered card states the five facts GREEN names, and both the props and the rendered markup are asserted not to leak -- a candidate-set owner renders as a generic protected-group phrase with `candidates:` and `sha256:` required absent from the emitted HTML, and a conflicted viewer's refusal names no second principal. **Boundaries.** The disposition card was not observed on screen: the dev corpus holds no approval work items, so `/workspace/app/work` renders `0 items`, and the card is proven instead by asserting the real rendered HTML through `ui.RenderToString` on the same server-rendered path this page uses. The assigned-person label humanizes a raw principal reference because no directory lookup is reachable from `productui`; a real display name is a larger, separate feature. `SeparationAuthority` protects the domain capability rather than a live endpoint, because EP-WORK-003's transport still has no production completion wiring -- a pre-existing gap already escalated, neither created nor worsened here -- and `execute.Driver.CompleteApproval` inherits the guarantee but has no production caller. Separately, `TestTodo_DB_EDGE_003_IntegrationPromotionCompositionRetriesSerializableAndRechecksApproval` had a hardcoded 20s budget that turned machine load into a false failure; confirmed pre-existing by running it in a worktree of unmodified HEAD, where it failed identically at 22.9s and 32.4s, and raised to 120s with every assertion unchanged

title: Replace free-text target positions with authorized vacancy selection and reservation evidence
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: an arbitrary guessed identifier such as `POS-ENG-MGR-101` is accepted without proving existence, vacancy, compatibility, effective-date capacity and reservation ownership
green: an accessible server-filtered picker shows only authorized compatible positions with title, organization, manager, location, vacancy window and reservation state; selection binds the immutable position revision; simulation explains advisory versus durable capacity; stale or concurrently reserved choices fail before approval with a recoverable alternative-selection state
refactor: the browser carries only the selected position revision reference; validation and reservation remain owned by Position
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Security` in `internal/domains/promotion` (`promoux004_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Race` in `internal/data/positionguard` (`guard_test.go`, `race_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Browser` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Accessibility` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux004_test.go`), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_WorkspaceLivePath` in `internal/intent/app` (`promoux004_test.go`); new `migrations/00287_promoux004_position_slot_guard.sql`, `internal/domains/position/revisionref.go`, `internal/domains/promotion/target_position.go`, `internal/domains/promotion/positionpicker`, `internal/data/positionguard`, `internal/data/positionfacts` and `internal/humanwork/productui/position_picker.go`. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 71.2% (`internal/domains/position`), 77.1% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 77.5% (`positionpicker`), 79.0% (`internal/data/positionguard`), 70.5% (`internal/data/positionfacts`), 98.6% (`internal/intent/definitions`), 72.1% (`internal/workflow/simulate`), 81.5% (`migrations`), 93.2% (`internal/humanwork/productui`) and 45.9% (`internal/intent/app`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. RED named a guessed identifier being accepted, so the decisive proof is that one is refused on the path a user actually reaches rather than in the evaluator alone. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_WorkspaceLivePath` composes a `Cell` the way a live deployment does, with a pgtest-backed `ExecutionDB` and tenant mapping, and drives `Cell.WorkspacePort().ReadPromotion`: a guessed `POS-ENG-MGR-101` comes back `StatusBlocked` with `CodeTargetPositionNotFound` and `Simulation.Executable == false`, the same refusal holds for an independently composed cell and tenant, and a request naming no position at all still reaches `StatusReady`. The check is no longer opt-in: any non-empty `TargetPlacement.PositionID` is decoded as a `position.RevisionRef` and evaluated, so a value that does not decode is refused on the existence ground. Each of the five grounds has its own subtest constructing a scenario where only that ground fails -- existence, compatibility, vacancy, effective-date revision currency and reservation ownership -- rather than a single invalid-position assertion that could pass with four of five wired. A bare identifier proves the first four; the fifth is a write and requires the richer `PositionSelection`, which is GREEN's advisory-versus-durable distinction. The reservation race is settled by the database: `promotion_target_position_guard_one_active_window`, a partial unique index on `(tenant_id, position_ref, effective_date) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'` that PostgreSQL evaluates as part of each `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING`'s own commit rather than by a read preceding the write, proven with 12 concurrent goroutines on independent connections. Enumeration is closed by passing the identical `position.Authorizer` to both the picker and the evaluator and requiring a guessed unauthorized position's `Finding` to be byte-for-byte identical to a genuinely nonexistent one's, so the refusal itself cannot be used to discover which position ids are real. Three real defects were found and fixed along the way. Ground four had used `CompareInStream`, which errors with `ErrRevisionNotOrdered` on the opaque revisions the real adapter mints; it now uses `Equal`, which is the exact binding REFACTOR asks for. Building the production `internal/data/positionfacts` adapter against real PostgreSQL surfaced a timezone bug -- date extraction did not normalize to UTC first, so a server in `America/New_York` shifted every date by up to a day -- and an off-by-one translating DB-009's exclusive `effective_to` boundary into the domain's inclusive end-date convention. One deliberate contract change: `target_position_ref` moved from `Required: true` to `Required: false` in `internal/intent/definitions`. The kernel had been stricter than the domain while proving less -- `checkPlacement` blocks on a missing target job code and grade but has never required a position, so the presence check only guaranteed a non-empty string and a guessed one satisfied it. A named position is now proven against the real Position domain, which is a stronger guarantee than presence ever gave, and job and grade remain blocking so the shape is not unconstrained. **Boundaries.** Ground five is never exercised on the live `journeyEngine.Propose` path: only the read-only preview reaches a wired `PositionReader`, and no caller yet supplies the `ProposalRef`/`IdempotencyKey`/`Reservations` a durable reservation needs, which would require real position rows seeded into the dev corpus and the commit path wired. `positionpicker` filters a caller-supplied candidate set because `position.PositionFacts` exposes no listing port; a real directory source is a separate feature. `TestTodo_MSRC_006_Golden` in `internal/intent/model/deferred` fails on a drifted DB-016 preview digest, confirmed unrelated here -- `go list -deps` shows `tools/gen/deferredschema` depends on none of the changed packages and generates its own content rather than reading the storage registry -- and escalated separately

title: Include reporting-line and organization impact in management promotions
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: a promotion into management can reach approval without resolving the target manager, organization, reporting-line edge, team impact and cycle check, or the review comparison omits those effects
green: position selection derives or explicitly collects authorized target organization and manager revisions; simulation proves the relationship rewrite and cycle safety; current/proposed review shows manager, organization, position and affected direct-report scope; material changes invalidate approval and re-run the exact checks
refactor: organization semantics stay in the Organization capability and promotion composes its typed effect rather than copying graph logic
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Security` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Golden` in `internal/domains/promotion` (`promoux005_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Integration` in `internal/data/orgfacts` (`reader_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Mutation` in `internal/data/promotioncommit` (`promoux005_mutation_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux005_test.go`); new `internal/domains/org/cycle.go`, `internal/data/orgfacts`, `internal/domains/promotion/target_manager.go` and `internal/humanwork/productui/promotion_review.go`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 76.3% (`internal/domains/org`), 78.8% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 75.9% (`internal/data/orgfacts`), 70.7% (`internal/data/promotioncommit`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 72.1% (`internal/workflow/simulate`) and 61.7% (`internal/humanwork/workspace`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised from 53.2%); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Cycle safety is real reachability rather than a single-hop guard. `org.DetectManagerCycle` walks the proposed manager's actual ancestor chain through `ResolveManagerRelationships` and asks whether the promoted worker appears in it, so a cycle that closes two or more hops up is caught; `TestDetectManagerCycle_MultiHop` and the PRIMARY's multi-hop subtest both build A reports to B reports to C and refuse promoting A to manage C, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Integration` reproduces that same shape against real PostgreSQL rows. The converse is proven too, because a check that refused every deep chain would pass a cycle test while breaking the product: `TestDetectManagerCycle_DeepChainAdmitted`, the PRIMARY's legitimate-deep-chain subtest and the Integration test's fourth worker all admit a four-hop chain that closes no cycle. The detector reports three outcomes rather than a boolean that would have to guess. A chain it cannot certify -- depth exceeded, a pre-existing loop above the proposed manager, a withheld disclosure, or a stale, disagreeing or ambiguous resolution -- returns UNDETERMINED, and promotion treats that as blocking with its own finding: `CycleSafe` requires both no cycle and no undetermined result, so an unresolved chain is never reported safe by omission. The materiality clause is proven to re-run the same checks rather than a cheaper subset: the PRIMARY runs `PreflightPromotion` twice changing only the affected-report scope, requires the inputs and result digests to move and the new run to find the cycle, and additionally requires **every pre-existing unrelated finding from the first run to reappear verbatim** -- so a re-validation that quietly dropped checks would fail. REFACTOR holds: the traversal lives in `internal/domains/org` and promotion composes its typed `ManagementImpact` effect rather than copying graph logic, with `internal/data/orgfacts` supplying the first production `org.WorkerFacts` adapter in the tree, reading `journey_worker`'s `manager_relationship_ref`. **A pre-existing defect was found and escalated rather than silently inherited.** Three commit-path cycle checks -- `org.ManagerMutation` at `manager_mutation.go:58`, `promotion/commit.Command` at `command.go:147` and `promotion/localcommit` at `localcommit.go:335` -- test membership in an ancestor list that nothing ever populates with a real resolution, so their self-reference half works while their multi-hop half always passes. They are dormant because P1A simulates `promote_worker` and never executes it, but they become silent no-ops the moment execution is enabled, which is why the Mutation test feeds a correctly computed list directly rather than pretending that path is wired. **Boundaries.** The HTTP form does not yet collect a target-manager selection, so the capability is composed end to end -- `Cell` to `orgfacts.Reader` to `PreflightRequest` -- but reachable only through the Go API today, the same shape PROMOUX-004 left for its durable reservation. The review card shows the manager as a raw worker id because no directory lookup is reachable from `productui`, the boundary PROMOUX-003 recorded. The full `test/bootstrap` and root suites were not run, per AGENTS.md's multi-hour guidance; every golden that actually broke was regenerated through its own package's `-update` flag

title: Show the authorized compensation baseline and exact entry guardrail before submit
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: the promotion form shows current base as `—` while enforcing a hidden percentage rule, or expresses only `0.0500..0.1800` after rejection
green: after target-role selection, authorized purpose-bound data displays current exact Money, permitted increase percent, exact minimum and maximum annual Money, band position, currency and effective-date basis; the input constrains and explains the range without floating-point arithmetic; unauthorized viewers receive a typed unavailable action rather than inferred pay
refactor: formatting uses shared Money and Percentage value types and locale services; the client never recomputes the authoritative guardrail
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) in `internal/domains/promotion` (`compensation_guardrail_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Browser`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Security` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_I18N` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`compensation_guardrail_test.go`), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Integration` in `internal/data/workforce` (`compensation_guardrail_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest); new `internal/domains/promotion/compensation_guardrail.go` and `internal/humanwork/productui/compensation_guardrail.go`; no migration and no new storage row required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 78.4% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 93.2% (`internal/humanwork/productui`) and 81.7% (`internal/data/workforce`); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. RED named a form expressing its guardrail as the raw range `0.0500..0.1800`, so the no-floating-point clause is proven by a test that would actually catch a float rather than by inspection. All money and percentage arithmetic lives in `permittedIncreasePercent`, using `Money.Sub` and `Decimal.Div` at a declared six-digit scale with `values.RoundingHalfEven` and no `float64` on the path; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006/NoFloatDrift` picks 1000000.03 and 1180000.09 -- the textbook double-precision trap scaled to salary figures -- and **first proves the trap is real on this platform**, failing with an explicit instruction to choose different cents if a float64 subtraction of those literals ever does reproduce 180000.06, before asserting the guardrail returns exactly 180000.06 and 0.180000. That self-validating shape means the test cannot silently decay into a vacuous assertion. The client is proven not to recompute the authoritative guardrail adversarially rather than agreeably: the Browser test supplies a projection whose maximum and permitted percent are deliberately not what `base * 1.18` or `(max - current) / current` would produce, and requires the rendered HTML to carry the supplied projection's exact strings rather than the recomputation. A well-formed fixture would have agreed either way and hidden a client-side calculation. The inference channel is closed in both layers, because a permitted range discloses the baseline -- a maximum of base times 1.18 lets a reader solve for base. At the domain, all six non-VALUE presence states (absent, null, unknown, redacted, unavailable, not-applicable) leave every data field zero and produce byte-identical `Canonical()` encodings, so the cause itself is not a signal. At the presentation, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Security` strips HTML tags -- so an `<h3>` cannot be mistaken for a leaked digit -- and requires zero digits, no percent sign and none of the authorized render's exact strings for both NOT_AUTHORIZED and BAND_UNRESOLVED, with an authorized control render proving the check is not vacuous. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_I18N` distinguishes locales rather than rendering three and asserting one string: en-US emits `550,000.00` where de-DE emits `550.000,00`, with grouping and decimal separators genuinely swapped for both money and percent, `USD` present in all three, and `ar` asserted RTL with Arabic-script text distinct from the English and German titles. **Boundaries.** No adapter in this tree implements `rewards.CompensationFacts` or `rewards.PayBandCatalog` against real PostgreSQL -- every production composition, including PROMOUX-004's and 005's, wires both from `internal/domains/fixtures` -- so the Integration test reaches real PostgreSQL for the part that has a real adapter, a worker's stored base pay, currency and pay basis through `workforce.Store` under row-level security, and composes that with an in-memory pay-band catalog. `internal/experience/localize` only swaps separators for `de` and `fr` prefixes, so Arabic numerals follow the en-US separator convention rather than Arabic-Indic digits; that is pre-existing and shared by every component using these value types. And the card is not rendered on any page a user reaches, the third such component after PROMOUX-003's approval disposition and PROMOUX-005's promotion review; all three are escalated together rather than left as three separate footnotes

title: Present promotion validation as field-linked recoverable guidance
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: a rejected pay value produces a page-level message containing field keys, decimal fractions, Go error names or correlation internals, does not associate the error with Proposed base pay, or leaves the user at an unrelated scroll position
green: typed refusal reasons map to localized field messages with exact corrective bounds; the summary links to each invalid field; focus and scroll move predictably without losing entered values; changing a field clears only its stale error; a copyable support reference is available through diagnostics without implementation text in ordinary copy
refactor: one refusal-to-presentation mapper serves SSR and enhanced clients; do not parse human error strings
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Golden`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Browser`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_I18N` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Security` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux007_test.go`); new `internal/humanwork/productui/promotion_validation.go`; `i18n.go` gained 37 `promotion_validation.*` keys per locale across en-US, de-DE and ar; no migration and no new storage row required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. No pre-existing test was modified. REFACTOR's two clauses are both structural rather than asserted. `MapPromotionRefusal` is the single refusal-to-presentation function, and it serves both render paths because SSR calls `ui.RenderToString(Build(view))` while the enhanced client calls `ui.Render(Build(view), selector)` -- the identical Go tree compiled twice, once native and once for js/wasm, so there is no second implementation that could drift. And it never parses human error strings: the mapper keys exclusively on `Finding.Code` and does not read `Finding.Message` anywhere, which matters because that is the field the domain itself documents as carrying raw decimal fractions, denial reasons and Go error text. Verified by inspection -- the only occurrences of `.Message` in the file are comments explaining why it is never read. The stale-error clause is proven with two invalid fields rather than one, because a single-field test cannot distinguish clearing one error from clearing all of them: the PRIMARY seeds `proposed.base` and `effective_date` as invalid, clears the first, and requires the second's issue to be unchanged in message, code, field and severity with exactly one issue remaining. The leak clause is proven in both directions, since asserting only that ordinary copy is clean could be satisfied by deleting the support reference entirely. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Security` renders a `Finding.Message` deliberately stuffed with a decimal fraction, a Go error string and a fake correlation id, strips tags, and requires none of it in visible copy -- while separately requiring the collapsed diagnostics panel to carry the exact `PreflightResult.ResultDigest`, an opaque hash the domain already computes, so support still has something to act on. Mapping is exhaustive and fails closed: all 32 `promotion.Finding` codes that exist today have explicit cases, a table-driven subtest asserts none of them reaches the fallback, and a separate subtest feeds an unrecognised code carrying an adversarial message and requires the output to be only the generic fallback text -- containing neither the code nor the leaked Go error text, decimal fraction or correlation string. Corrective bounds are quoted from PROMOUX-006's guardrail rather than recomputed: `CodeBelowBandMinimum` and `CodeAboveBandMaximum` render `MinimumAnnualized` and `MaximumAnnualized` through the shared money helper with no arithmetic in this layer, and an unavailable guardrail falls back to a bound-free message proven digit-free. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_I18N` distinguishes locales rather than rendering three and asserting one string: the quoted bound's grouping and decimal separators swap between en-US `500,000.00` and de-DE `500.000,00`, the surrounding sentence itself differs, and the Arabic render carries real Arabic-script characters distinct from both. **Boundary.** The mapper and its components are not wired into any page a user reaches, because no live promotion-proposal form exists yet in `internal/transport/journey` or `tools/uxqual/render/journey`. This is the fourth such component after PROMOUX-003's approval disposition, PROMOUX-005's promotion review and PROMOUX-006's compensation guardrail; all four are covered by the single escalation raised at PROMOUX-006 rather than recorded as separate footnotes. It was deliberately built to the shape those precedents established -- a server-resolved verdict with a presentation-only projection -- so the wiring is additive rather than a rewrite. The wasm hydration path is proven structurally identical rather than executed, since no browser was used here

title: Put promotion machinery behind an authorized diagnostics disclosure
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: ordinary promotion review exposes entity refs, material or plan digests, raw `SET` operations, workflow node names, work-item UUIDs, raw event codes, principals or `JourneyService` labels by default
green: the default page shows employee, proposed business changes, approvals, policy explanations, effective date, next owner and human-readable history; an authorized Technical details disclosure contains identifiers, evidence and trace references with copy controls and redaction; unauthorized viewers cannot infer hidden internals from presence, count or layout
refactor: business timeline events and diagnostic evidence are two projections over the same immutable records, not duplicated stored summaries
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Golden` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Accessibility` in `tools/uxqual/render/journey` (`promoux008_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Security` in `internal/transport/journey` (`promoux008_test.go`), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Browser` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_I18N` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux008_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 97.0% (`internal/experience/roleaccess`), 80.9% (`internal/transport/journey`), 96.6% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`), 87.1% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`) and 93.4% (`internal/humanwork/productui`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. RED reproduced on two independent surfaces before the change. The `Technical details` disclosure in `tools/uxqual/render/journey/components.go` was rendered at two sites, both gated on nothing but `htmlIf(j.WorkerRef != "" || j.InstanceID != "", ...)` -- data presence, with no role, capability or purpose check anywhere in the path -- so every viewer who could see a journey card received `eref:v1:harborcare-demo:worker:0e30e81f-984f-5611-8570-f8c903470020` and an instance UUID, and GREEN asks for an _authorized_ disclosure. That same predicate was also the inference channel GREEN's third clause forbids, because the summary's presence was a direct function of whether internals existed; gating only the contents would have left it open. Separately `/workspace/app/work` rendered a raw work-item UUID (`01a09a09-074d-7b2d-9dc9-409e252ec222`) in its default view on a page carrying zero `<details>` elements at all, which is the RED's "work-item UUIDs" clause verbatim. Diagnostics authority is now a first-class page id, `journey-diagnostics`, carried as the same wire string through `roleaccess.PageJourneyDiagnostics`, `productui.PageJourneyDiagnostics` and `journeyclient.diagnosticsPageID`, granted to `hcm_admin`/`comp_admin` through their existing blanket grant and to `promotion_operator` explicitly, and to nobody else -- managers and HR partners who can approve a promotion still cannot read its machinery. The server gate (`internal/transport/journey/diagnostics_access.go`) fails **closed**: a nil RoleAccess store, an empty permission table and an absent explicit grant all deny, deliberately unlike the pre-existing `requirePageAction`'s permissive rolling-upgrade default, because this authority never existed before and a permissive default would have silently granted it to everyone. Identifiers are withheld from the **payload**, not merely from the view: `convert.go`'s `toJourney`, `toInstance`, `toDetail` and `toWorkItem` drop `MaterialDigest`, `CorrelationId`, `InstanceId`/`InstanceVersion`, the whole `Instance` message, `PlannedWrites`, `Ledger`, `EvidenceIds`, `Nodes`, `Transitions` and every `WorkItem.WorkItemId` for an unauthorized caller across `ListJourneys`, `ProposeJourney`, `InspectJourney`, `ExecuteJourney`, `DecideJourney` and `WatchJourney`. `WorkerRef` and `IntentID` are deliberately kept for every viewer because they are the routing keys the person-profile link and the journey's own address need, and the live check confirms that is all they are used for. The presence channel is closed by a server-derived `JourneyCard.DiagnosticsAuthorized` computed once via `cfg.CanPageAction("journey-diagnostics", "view")`, never from data presence; the detail page's `workflowSection`, `outcomeSection` and `evidenceSection`, which had rendered unconditionally whenever they held content, are gated the same way -- a defect the first evidence pass missed because it scanned only the list page. **Live matrix.** Signed in as the `admin` persona and again as a `promotion_operator`-only credential, `/workspace/app/journeys` renders 9 `Technical details` disclosures whose contents are redacted to `Worker ••••0020` and `Instance ••••9d08` with zero full UUIDs visible and two copy controls carrying the distinct accessible names `Copy Worker value` and `Copy Instance value`, the buttons writing the unredacted value through `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. Signed in as the `hiring-manager` persona (`hiring_manager`, `manager`, `intent_author`), the same page renders **0** disclosures, 0 UUIDs and 0 `eref:` occurrences in visible text, and every UUID remaining anywhere in the markup is a `href="#/journeys/<id>"` routing address -- a scan for a UUID outside an `href` attribute returned none. `/workspace/app/work` likewise fell from one raw UUID in visible text to zero for that persona. Because unauthorized viewers receive `detailsCount: 0` uniformly, there is no per-journey variation left to infer from. title: Canonicalize and deduplicate promotion simulation findings
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: one budget observation appears twice with swapped internal code and message, or ordering and identity change across reloads
green: findings have a stable semantic identity, owner, severity, affected field/effect and one canonical explanation; exact duplicates collapse while independently sourced corroboration remains attributable; deterministic ordering and count survive persistence and reload
refactor: deduplication operates on typed finding identity before presentation, never on rendered strings
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Property`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Golden`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Mutation` in `internal/domains/promotion/simcontract` (`promoux009_test.go`), plus `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Browser` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (`promoux009_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 75.1% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 79.0% (`internal/domains/promotion/simcontract`) and 87.1% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. This todo could not be reproduced in a browser: findings are produced by a simulation and every live journey sits past that stage, so nothing was on screen to inspect and producing one would have meant proposing a promotion that mutates tenant state. The defect was therefore established from the contract and proved by driving the real rule engine in test. `promotion.Finding` (`preflight.go:134`) carried only `Code`, `Severity`, `Field` and `Message` -- no owner at all, though GREEN names owner as part of the identity -- and nothing anywhere deduplicated: `sortFindings` (`preflight.go:200`) is a total order over `(Code, Field, Message)` that collapses nothing, and `simcontract.Assemble` did a straight `clone(in.Findings)`, with eight independent append sites feeding findings across the domain. Ordering was therefore already deterministic and was left alone; the half of RED about ordering changing across reloads did not reproduce. `Finding` now carries `Owner` and `CorroboratedBy`, and `DeduplicateFindings` groups by a typed `FindingIdentity` of `(Code, Field, Severity)` before presentation, never on rendered strings, picking the canonical `Message` deterministically so replay order cannot change the surviving explanation. `Owner` is deliberately outside the identity: two owners reporting one `(Code, Field, Severity)` are independently sourced corroboration of a single observation rather than two observations, so they collapse to one row whose every contributing owner is recorded, while a same-owner repeat collapses with an empty `CorroboratedBy`. Dedup runs inside `Assemble`, strictly upstream of `deriveStatus` and `computeDigest` and therefore of `Persist`, so the digest cannot vary with how many times a rule happened to fire and the reloaded count is exactly the assembled one. **A first implementation of this todo was sent back, and the reason is worth recording.** It defined the identity as `(Field, Severity)` alone, excluding `Code` on the reasoning that RED's "swapped internal code and message" meant neither field could be trusted. That silently discarded genuinely distinct observations: `checkCompensation` (`rules.go`) raises both `CodeProposedAmountInvalid` and `CodeNotARaise` on `Field` `proposed.base` at `SeverityBlocking` for a single proposal carrying a present-but-zero proposed base against a positive current base, because the early return guards only `!currentOK || !proposedOK` and a zero amount leaves `proposedOK` true. Under that identity the two collapsed into one and the lexicographically smaller pair won, so the reviewer was told the amount was not a raise and never told it was invalid. The same collision shape exists on `target.grade` (`CodeTargetGradeRequired` and `CodeSameGrade`) and on `proposed.base.currency` (`CodeCurrencyRequired` and `CodeCurrencyChangeNotV0`), and nothing enforces that such pairs stay mutually exclusive as rules are added. `Code` is a small closed vocabulary of rule-assigned typed constants, not a display string, so it belongs in the identity; `Message` is the freeform field REFACTOR's "never on rendered strings" is about, and it stays out. RED's swapped case now resolves on its own terms: the same `Code` with differing wording is a true duplicate and collapses, while genuinely differing `Code` means two rules fired and both are surfaced honestly rather than reconciled by guessing which message belongs to which code -- which would be rendered-string matching one level up. The regression test drives the real `promotion.PreflightPromotion` over a real `PreflightRequest` rather than a hand-built literal, and asserts the fixture actually reproduces both codes before asserting both survive, so it cannot quietly become vacuous if the rules change. **I mutation-verified that fix myself rather than relying on the lane's report**: reverting `Finding.Identity()` to `(Field, Severity)` failed `real_compensation_findings_survive_distinct_codes_on_one_field` with `Findings on proposed.base after dedup = [...], want exactly 2` and `distinct_codes_sharing_field_and_severity_are_never_merged` likewise, and restoring the line returned the package to green. The PROPERTY test was rebuilt for the same trap it had fallen into -- it had passed under the broken identity because its generator only ever produced genuine duplicates -- and now seeds every trial with a confusable neighbour carrying a different `Code` on a shared field and severity, failing at trial 0 under the reverted identity. **Boundary.** Nothing yet wires real preflight output into `AssembleInput.Findings` (`managerchange/setup.go` never sets it), so the roughly forty `Finding{...}` sites in `rules.go`, `target_manager.go` and `target_position.go` were left with an empty `Owner` rather than speculatively tagged, and `journeyv1.Finding` on the wire carries only severity, code and message -- no field or owner -- so typed dedup structurally cannot happen at that layer and the BROWSER test instead pins that the render layer is a faithful passthrough preserving order and count without re-deduplicating on strings

title: Keep promotion review confirmations compact, visible and keyboard-stable
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: expanding Start, Approve or Reject pushes the final action below the viewport, moves unrelated sections, loses focus or makes Cancel the most visually prominent control
green: a shared review surface keeps employee, change, date, consequences and final action together; the action bar remains visible; focus enters and returns correctly; Escape cancels; reduced motion is honored; server latency produces an in-place busy state that prevents duplicate submission without collapsing geometry
refactor: Start, Approve, Reject, Withdraw and Cancel reuse one confirmation component with typed content props
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Browser`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Performance` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Regression` in `tools/uxqual/render/journey` (`promoux010_test.go`), plus a second `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Regression` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (`promoux010_test.go`) proving the wiring; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 96.5% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`) and 87.4% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **RED reproduced live before any change** at 1024x768 on the Start path: clicking `Propose promotion for Peter` left the submit control at document top 1241 in a 768px viewport with `scrollY` 0 (473px below the fold), shifted two `<section>` elements by +37px and -54px while document height collapsed from 4984 to 1423, and dropped `document.activeElement` to `BODY`. The review surface contained exactly one button, so RED's fourth clause -- Cancel being the most prominent control -- was false only because no cancel affordance existed at all, and `keydown`/`Escape` dispatched at both `document` and `document.body` changed nothing. **Verified live after the change, as this section's preamble requires**, rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. One `reviewSurface` component now serves every consequential action through typed content props, keeping the pre-existing `<details>`/`<summary>` disclosure byte-for-byte as the zero-JS baseline so `TestConsequentialActionRequiresAReviewDisclosure` passes unmodified, and using GWC's own `ui.Overlay` modal primitive for the focus trap rather than hand-rolling one. Opening it moves nothing outside itself: `sectionsMoved` 0 with document height 1427 before and after, the surface computing `position:fixed`, `max-height:736px` (100vh minus 2rem) and `overflow-y:auto`, its action bar holding Cancel at 3232px² against Submit at 7101px² so the destructive-adjacent control is 2.2x the visual weight of cancel, both at top 634 and inside the viewport. `Escape` closes it completely: `details.open` false, the surface removed, document height unchanged and `document.activeElement` back to `SUMMARY#propose-review-trigger` with focus returned to the exact trigger that opened it. **Three passes were sent back, and the reasons are the record.** The first built the component but wired it to nothing: `Action.Confirmation` was set in `projector.go` for Approve and Reject while `ProposalForm.Confirmation` was set by no caller at all, so the live Start path still rendered its submit in a plain `div.jn-formfoot` with zero `<details>` and zero `[class*=confirm]` elements -- the lane had reasoned that wiring lay outside this todo's Refs, and Refs name where work centers rather than fencing an unrendered component into a closed todo. The second wired it but left the entry point unreachable: after the fix the surface's own trigger sat at top 1252 with `scrollY` 0, 484px below the fold and within 5px of the original defect, so the clause stood. The third targeted focus at the page heading, which could never have closed it -- the heading renders at top 143, already inside the viewport and above the trigger, so focusing it cannot scroll anything into view; that was established by measuring both positions rather than by argument, and separately by confirming that one `.focus()` on the trigger itself moved `scrollY` from 0 to 666 and brought it to top 586 through the browser's own scroll-on-focus, with no scroll call. **The fourth pass also found why the effect had not been firing at all, and it is a genuine GWC hazard this repository already documents.** GWC hooks are positional and attach to `GetCurrentFiber()`, and only a `ui.CreateElement` boundary creates a fiber -- a plain nested function call does not. The focus hook had been invoked as a plain call inside `proposalView`, itself reached only through `LiveComponent.Build`'s `List`/`Proposal`/`Detail` switch, so it landed in whatever slot that single flat hook sequence happened to reach on a render whose shape changes with every page transition; `live.go`'s own doc comment warns about exactly this. Wrapping it as `ui.CreateElement(focusOnMount, ...)` gives it its own reconciled fiber. Live, the effect now fires on the `Page.List` to `Page.Proposal` swap: `document.activeElement` is `SUMMARY#propose-review-trigger`, `scrollY` is 659, and the trigger sits at top 587 inside the viewport, against `BODY` and top 1252 before. The page heading keeps its id and `tabindex="-1"` for screen-reader route announcement, which is the right target for that job and the wrong one for this geometry. The lane also caught a vacuous assertion in its own test while mutation-checking: retargeting the focus id back to the heading left the markup subtest passing, because both ids exist in the output regardless of which one the effect is told to focus, so a `focusOnMountHook` spy was added to assert the argument rather than the rendered ids -- the same build-it-but-do-not-wire-it shape as the first pass, caught one level down. **Residuals, named rather than smoothed over.** Clicking Start still swaps `Page.List` to `Page.Proposal` wholesale (document height 4971 to 1427); re-architecting that spans `journeywasm` routing, is high blast-radius, and is deliberately not this todo -- what this todo fixes is that the review-and-submit step reached by that swap is now contained, cancellable, keyboard-stable and in view. `Action.Busy` and `ProposalForm.Busy` are real tested props but no production caller sets them yet, so GREEN's in-place busy state is structurally present and not yet live; wiring it belongs where `journeyclient`'s store turns an `OnSubmit` click into an RPC and back, is not part of PROMOUX-013's authorization semantics, and is filed separately. Reduced motion is covered by the sheet's existing blanket `prefers-reduced-motion` rule rather than a new one

title: Invalidate promotion counts and timestamps after every durable transition
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: after creating or approving a promotion the shell still announces zero journeys, `Updated` remains older than the newest transition, or views converge only after unrelated navigation
green: each committed promotion transition emits one authority-filtered invalidation with sequence; shell count, Journeys, My Work, Person and detail refresh only their affected regions; displayed last-updated time equals the latest business transition; reconnect catch-up converges without duplicate renders or lost scroll/focus
refactor: consumers share cache keys and sequence handling; no page triggers a full-shell reload to achieve consistency
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Performance` in `internal/domains/promotion` (`promoux011_test.go`, `promoux011_performance_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Race` in `internal/data/promotioninvalidation` (`sequence_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux011_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Recovery` in `tools/uxqual/invalidation` (`promoux011_test.go`); new `migrations/00288_promoux011_transition_sequence.sql`, `internal/data/promotioninvalidation` and `internal/domains/promotion/promoux011.go`. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.4% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 88.9% (`internal/data/promotioninvalidation`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 86.6% (`tools/uxqual/invalidation`), 81.7% (`internal/data/schema`), 100.0% (`internal/data/tenancy/storagedisposition`) and 81.5% (`migrations`); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED and driftgate and apigate pass on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. No pre-existing test file was edited. The clause that carries this todo is that an authority-filtered invalidation carries a sequence, and those two requirements interact as a disclosure bug rather than a cosmetic one: with a global sequence and a filter that merely drops undeliverable messages, a viewer who observes 1, 2, 4 has learned that event 3 exists and can count promotions they hold no authority over. The scheme chosen is gap-free renumbering per subscriber. `promotioninvalidation.NextSequence` allocates each committed transition a durable global position through `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`, evaluated inside each writer's own commit so concurrent writers cannot lose or duplicate one, but that value never reaches the wire -- it serves only as an item's revision for stale and reorder protection. `SubscriberSequencer.EmitForSubscriber` mints each subscriber its own counter and advances it by exactly one **only when a message is actually delivered**, so a transition authorising nothing for that subscriber never touches their counter and their visible sequence is contiguous by construction. The proof reproduces the leak before fixing it, which is what distinguishes it from a test that merely asserts the corrected behaviour: the PRIMARY's `subscriber_sequencer_closes_the_disclosure_gap_the_naive_scheme_leaks` subtest first runs the naive scheme and observes the delivered pair `[1, 3]` with a gap of 2, then runs the real one and requires `[1, 2]` with a delta of exactly 1. Region isolation is proven against real `tools/uxqual/invalidation.Client` instances rather than a stub: a Detail-region message for one worker fires exactly the matching client once and leaves a My-Work client and a different worker's Detail client at zero, so REFACTOR's prohibition on a full-shell reload is enforced rather than assumed. Last-updated is proven equal to the newest transition's own `OccurredAt` regardless of input order, with an empty set rendering an empty string rather than falling back to the current time. The no-duplicate-render clause is counted rather than inferred, because a double render converges to the same state and would pass any state assertion: the Recovery test counts `Refetch` invocations across a reconnect that redelivers an already-applied sequence before a genuinely new one, and requires exactly two. The Performance entry asserts delivered-message counts and bounded per-subscriber state rather than elapsed time, deliberately avoiding this machine's unreliable wall-clock behaviour. Zero values fail closed throughout: `RegionCursor{}` refuses any incoming value including 0, `Transition{}` and zero-revision or zero-timestamp variants fail `Validate()`, and the sequencer never advances on an undelivered message. **A defect I introduced was found by this lane and corrected here.** The `ledger_payload_disposition` row I added during PROMOUX-002 review declared `data_role: EVIDENCE` and `retention_class: EVIDENCE`, neither of which is a declared value -- `data_role` admits only LEDGER, PROJECTION, OUTBOX, REGISTRY, CONTROL and AGGREGATE, and `retention_class` only PERMANENT, OPERATIONAL and REBUILDABLE. It broke `TestTodo_STORE_001` and `TestTodo_STORE_001_Mutation` and had escaped notice because that gate lives in `internal/data/tenancy/storagedisposition`, a different package from the `TestTodo_DATA_001` check run at the time. Corrected to LEDGER and PERMANENT, matching `ledger_event` itself. **Boundaries.** The components are not wired into a live promotion page, the same boundary PROMOUX-003, 005, 006 and 007 recorded and which is escalated for all of them together; no production caller yet invokes `NextSequence` from a committed-transition write path, which lies outside this todo's Refs. DOM scroll and focus preservation on reconnect is asserted structurally -- region containers are independently addressable -- because it cannot be proven in a non-browser Go test, and the Recovery test says so in its own comment

section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: `Waiting for effective date` gives no next timestamp, timezone, owner, scheduled action or explanation, and the supported local-dev profile cannot exercise terminal recording without waiting for wall-clock time
green: the waiting state names the effective instant and timezone, what will run, remaining checks, notification behavior and any authorized intervention; production exposes no manual timer bypass; a separately fenced local-dev clock/driver can advance a same-day fixture through END and is impossible to enable under a production profile

evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) in `internal/intent/app` (`wait_explain_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Integration` in `internal/application` (`promoux014_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Recovery` in `internal/application` (`promoux014_recovery_test.go`, `//go:build devtools`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Security` in `internal/platform/devclock` (`promoux014_security_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Browser` in `tools/uxqual/render/journey` (`promoux014_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Regression` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (`promoux014_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 46.1% (`internal/intent/app`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised from 45.4% by this change), 100.0% (`internal/platform/devclock` default build), 96.6% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`), 87.5% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`), 94.4% (`internal/workflow/promotionexec`) and 81.3% (`internal/application`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `go build -tags devtools ./internal/platform/devclock/` and `go vet -tags devtools` clean, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **RED reproduced live before the change.** A `WAITING_EFFECTIVE_DATE` card on the running server rendered only `Waiting for effective date`, the placement and pay lines, `Effective 1 Dec 2026` and `Updated 2026-09-13 08:25 UTC`: of RED's five facts the next timestamp was a bare date rather than an instant, and the timezone, owner, scheduled action and explanation were absent outright. Three journeys sit in that stage, so the gap was against real data rather than a fixture. The second half reproduced too -- a sweep of non-test code for a clock driver found only `internal/data/health`'s `FakeClock`, a health-projection concern, and a doc-comment mention in `internal/platform/timeauth`, so nothing could advance a promotion's wait and the local-dev profile could not reach terminal recording without wall-clock time. All five facts are now server-sourced and none is computed in the browser: the instant and timezone come from the durable pending timer's `FiresAt` (`internal/workflow/timer.Scheduler.Pending`) paired with `promotionexec.EffectiveDateZoneID`, verified against the real engine to resolve a `2026-06-01` effective date to `2026-06-01T04:00:00Z` under America/New*York; the owner is the latest completed `APPROVAL` work item's `CompletedBy`; the scheduled action is read from `promotionexec.Definition().Edges`' real `FIRED` route out of the wait node rather than hardcoded prose; and the remaining checks, notification behaviour and intervention statements describe what the engine actually does. The proposer is deliberately **not** shown as owner, because that would require `IntentInstance.Initiator`, which has no wire slot on `Journey` or `JourneyDetail` -- named rather than approximated. Because `schema/proto` and `gen/` are frozen, the six facts travel as `WAIT*\*`codes through the existing generic`JourneyDetail.Findings`vessel, and the client filters them out of the generic preflight board into their own labelled subsection instead of letting them inflate it. **The fence is the security-critical half and is structural, not merely checked.** The driver lives behind a`devtools`build tag: the default`driver_stub.go`never imports`timer.Scheduler.Fire`, so the capability is absent from `cmd/hcmnext`'s ordinary build, from CI and from the amd64 cross-compile, rather than present and refused. `devprofile.Name`-gated construction is defence in depth on top, fail-closed with exact-match only, and an unexported `ready`field leaves even a hand-constructed`Driver{}`literal inert. The driver wraps exactly the production`timer.Scheduler.Fire`and`executionscheduler.Scheduler.Tick`path rather than duplicating engine logic. All six tests were mutation-verified: removing the`Kind != KindApproval`filter in`lastApprovalOwner`failed the PRIMARY naming the leak; disabling the`Inspect`attach block emptied all six findings and failed the INTEGRATION; changing the subsection heading failed the BROWSER; making the stub's`fireNow`branch on tenant failed the SECURITY's byte-identical check; dropping`.Add(ahead)`from the dev clock failed the RECOVERY with`Fired 0 want 1`; and removing the all-codes-present guard in `waitExplanationFacts`failed the REGRESSION on both its partial and absent sub-cases. **Live-verification boundary, recorded rather than glossed.** Unlike section 69, this section carries no direct-browser-evidence requirement, and three independent constraints blocked a live read of the rendered panel: signing in from the browser pane is refused with`the request origin is not allowed`, because the pane's sandboxed iframe Origin fails `originAllowed`; `/workspace/journey` runs under a fixed local-dev identity (`hc-054-thomas-baker`, `promotion_operator`) whose organization scope cannot open any of the three waiting journeys, each answering `This journey is unavailable`; and the Connect RPC is not exposed on the plain HTTP listener, answering `404`at`/hcmnext.journey.v1.JourneyService/InspectJourney`because it is reachable only through the`/workspace/grpc`tunnel. The INTEGRATION test against real PostgreSQL is therefore what proves the server attaches these findings on real data, and the BROWSER test is what proves the renderer displays them. **Gap, named:** the driver is not wired into`serve.go`or`handler.go`-- both fenced off this session by another todo's uncommitted work -- so today it is consumable through`go test -tags devtools` rather than a CLI
